tools.name: find_component
tools.description: Finds the component for a UI need described in plain words, ranked, and says when this catalog ships nothing on purpose because the phone's own control is the right choice. Omit `need` to list every component with its purpose and whether it renders the real system control.

tools.name: get_component
tools.description: Everything needed to write a correct call site for one component: props with types, defaults and allowed values, what draws on iOS and on Android, the providers it needs at the app root, its dependencies, and the runtime rules that stop it rendering blank.

tools.name: check_snippet
tools.description: Scans TSX that uses these components for the mistakes that render nothing with no error: animated opacity on glass, the flex: 1 collapse, a clipped lens, a conditionally mounted surface. A read-only text scan, not a guarantee; verify_app checks a whole emitted project.

tools.name: get_app_setup
tools.description: How an app is set up so these components work and follow its theme, one topic at a time: the app-root providers in the order that works, the theme hooks and token scales, or the rules that hold across the whole catalog. An app built by emit_app already has all three wired.

tools.name: emit_app
tools.description: Needs a subscription. Turns a design from the Designer into a working Expo app: navigation, providers, tab bar, screens and the components they use. Returns a recipe for the current project: every file with its target path, one install line and ordered steps with a check each. Pass `step` for one st

tools.name: add_screen
tools.description: Needs a subscription. Adds one screen designed in the Designer to a project. With the project's .opointo/files.json it returns the screen file, the route that mounts it and the one line to register it, and never rewrites existing files. Without it, a self-contained screen file for any Expo app.

tools.name: install_component
tools.description: Needs a subscription, except for the free foundation components. Adds one component to an existing project: the files it and its dependencies need in install order with exact target paths, the single expo install line, the providers it needs and its runtime rules. A backend recipe's id, such as "sup

tools.name: update_components
tools.description: Needs a subscription. Reads the project's .opointo/files.json and returns only the opointo-supplied files that changed since export, so it works months later with no share code. Never touches the customer's own screens, and flags the rare change that needs a code edit rather than a copy.

tools.name: verify_app
tools.description: Needs a subscription. Checks an emitted app before it is built: missing files, altered verbatim files, absent packages, the expo-router config merge, whether the installed Xcode can build it, and whether a change needs a new native build.

tools.name: propose_app
tools.description: Your agent can design an app with you: send an app in opointo's design format (the AppSpec emit_app builds from) and get back a link that opens it in the Designer as a new, unsaved design. The person sees every screen, changes what they like, and hands it back for emit_app. into: the code in the per

tools.name: propose_screen
tools.description: Your agent can design a single screen with you: send one screen in opointo's design format (the Composition add_screen builds from) and get back a link that opens it in the Designer as a new, unsaved design the person can change. into: as propose_app's. dryRun checks without making a link; format: t

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "check_snippet" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "emit_app" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
